data.body:
AC1 NOW SATISFIED - the missing construct-uniqueness guard landed as Gerrit 2082 (merged). This is the criterion that blocked this ticket's close: the consolidation shipped without the guard its own AC1 names, so nothing failed when a fourth copy of the duplicates/supersedes walk reappeared.

The guard is tests/unit/commands/test_replacement_walker.py::test_the_replacement_link_walk_has_exactly_one_body. It scans every file under src/rebar except the owner close_disposition.py and matches the CONJUNCTION of 'find_inbound_relationships(' and '"supersedes"'. The conjunction is load-bearing: several modules legitimately call find_inbound_relationships for unrelated questions and 'supersedes' is just a link relation name, so matching either atom alone would fire on innocent code, and a guard that cries wolf gets deleted. A legitimate second walk escapes with '# replacement-walk-ok: <why>' on an atom's line, reason MANDATORY.

TEETH PROVEN BY MUTATION, three ways, each applied to live code and reverted: (1) an unmarked copy appended to _store/hlc.py FAILS the guard, naming the offending file; (2) the same copy with '# replacement-walk-ok: probe' PASSES; (3) the same copy with a bare reasonless '# replacement-walk-ok:' FAILS again. A companion test asserts the owner itself carries a reasoned marker and that a reasonless one is rejected.

Also fixed along the way: my first version of the marker regex omitted re.MULTILINE, so '$' only matched at end-of-file and the owner-marker assertion failed against the whole file text. Caught by the test itself. Full suite: 11 passed.
